title: PrimeBOT Builds Its 10,000th Personal Robot, 14 Days After Its 5,000th
summary: PrimeBOT says its 10,000th Q1 and T1 personal robot rolled off the line on November 8, with daily capacity at 240 units. It has not disclosed sales or deliveries.
points: PrimeBOT, the personal-robot brand of Shanghai-listed Swancor Advanced Materials, said its 10,000th robot came off the production line on November 8.
The 5,000th unit was completed on October 25, so the second batch of 5,000 took 14 days.
PrimeBOT began handing over its first robots on October 1 in seven Chinese cities, including Shanghai, Shenzhen and Hangzhou, according to Global Times .

title: Atlas Battery Pack to Use 70 Samsung SDI Cells, Report Says
summary: The reported 1.3 kWh pack adds detail to Atlas’s power system as humanoid makers pursue battery swapping, fast charging and new chemistries.
points: Samsung SDI is supplying the battery cells for Boston Dynamics’ Atlas humanoid, with each robot using 70 cylindrical cells in a pack of approximately 1.3 kWh, according to The Elec .
The report offers a closer look at the power supply behind Atlas as robot manufacturers pursue different ways to keep their machines working through an industrial shift.
The reported cells have a capacity of 5,000 mAh each and use the 2170 format: 21 mm in diameter and 70 mm long.

title: Robot Talk Episode 169 – Robot sensing inspired by nature, with Dexter Shepherd
summary: Claire chatted to Dexter Shepherd from the University of Sussex about using artificial intelligence to help robots understand and adapt to their environment. Dexter Shepherd is a Postdoctoral Research
points: Dexter Shepherd is a Postdoctoral Researcher at the University of Sussex, exploring machine learning for bio-inspired tactile sensing and robotic locomotion.
His work combines embedded AI systems, spatial-temporal models, and reinforcement learning to enable robots to classify textures, orient themselves, and adapt their movements.

title: Swiss Startup Embodied AI Unveils AIR, a Wheeled Robot Built to Work Beside Factory Staff Without a Cage
summary: The EPFL spin-off's two-armed robot starts each job under remote control and, the company says, takes the task over within a month. It reports a 95% average success rate in paid pilots.
points: Embodied AI, a 25-person startup spun out of Swiss technical university EPFL, has unveiled AIR, a two-armed robot on a wheeled base that the company says can work beside factory staff without a safety cage.
CEO Francesco Stella is presenting the robot today at Humanoid Europe 2026 in Munich, and the company says it will open orders after the unveiling.
Stella, 28, earned his robotics PhD at EPFL and did research at MIT.

title: Tokyo Researchers Build Robotic Legs With 3D-Printed Muscles, Tendons and Ligaments
summary: University of Tokyo researchers combine flexible printed structures with motor-driven wires to demonstrate supported stepping, offering a different take on bio-inspired robotics from Clone.
points: University of Tokyo researchers have built a life-size robotic leg system with 3D-printed structures inspired by muscles, tendons and ligaments.
Their approach uses one flexible plastic, changing its geometry to give different parts different mechanical properties.
Shunnosuke Yoshimura, Kento Kawaharazuka and Kei Okada describe the work in Advanced Intelligent Systems , where it was published on September 11.
